issues.description: ExcellenceLand constructor parameter order in the solution does not follow the ordering rule required by the problem statement. The problem/UML list the attributes (excellencyLevel: double, excellentEnough: boolean) and the problem text additionally requires a private List<Ride> rides attribute. The solution declares the constructor as ExcellenceLand(List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel) — placing rides first and reversing the order of excellencyLevel and excellentEnough. This contradicts the problem's explicit instruction that constructors must accept attributes in the same order as in the UML diagram (and for added attributes, they should be positioned consistently with the specification). Students following the specification would implement a different constructor signature and will be unable to match the solution's signature, causing confusion and potential test failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the ExcellenceLand constructor parameters follow the UML / problem-statement attribute order. For example: public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) { this.excellencyLevel = excellencyLevel; this.excellentEnough = excellentEnough; this.rides = rides; } This ensures students implementing the constructor per instructions match the intended API and tests.
